SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.error: Gives the wrong opposite (thinks the opposite of north is east or west).

example.question: Which point is opposite north on a compass?
example.correct_answer: South

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.cause: The child reads the four points as a list, not as two straight lines crossing.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.reveals: Offer "East" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.help: Draw a plus sign: north at the top, south at the bottom, east and west across. Ask for the point straight across.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.feedback: North and south are opposite, and east and west are opposite. The opposite point is straight across the compass.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.error: Swaps east and west (thinks that facing north, east is on the left).

example.question: You face north. Which side is east on?
example.correct_answer: The right hand

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.cause: The child pictures the compass on a page instead of standing in it.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.reveals: Offer "The left hand" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.help: Have the child stand and face north, stretch out the right arm and say "east". Then turn and do it again.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.feedback: Face north and east is on your right hand. West is on your left hand.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.error: Thinks the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, or rises in the north.

example.question: In which direction does the sun rise?
example.correct_answer: The east

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.cause: The child remembers the sun being high or low but not the side.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.reveals: Offer "The west" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.help: Watch the sun rise on a school morning and name the side; use it to find east and then the other points.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.feedback: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.error: Gives the direction the wrong way round (school is north of the market, so says the market is north of the school).

example.question: A school is north of a market. In which direction is the market from the school?
example.correct_answer: South

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.cause: The child repeats the word in the sentence and does not turn round to the other place.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.reveals: Offer "North" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.help: Put two objects on the desk. Ask "from this one to that one", then swap and ask again.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.feedback: If the school is north of the market, then the market is south of the school. Turn the direction round.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.error: Gets the direction wrong after a turn (facing east and turning left gives south).

example.question: Wanjiku faces east and turns left. Which direction does she face now?
example.correct_answer: North

SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.cause: The child turns the wrong way or does not picture facing the direction.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.reveals: Offer "South" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.help: Have the child stand and face a wall called east, then turn a quarter turn left and name the new wall.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.feedback: Facing east, a turn to the left faces north. A turn to the right would face south.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Thinks a sub-county is bigger than a county.

example.question: Which is bigger, a county or a sub-county?
example.correct_answer: A county

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child knows both names and not which holds the other.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "A sub-county" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Use boxes inside boxes: the county box holds several sub-county boxes, which hold wards.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: A county is divided into sub-counties. Many sub-counties make one county, so the county is bigger.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Puts county, sub-county and ward in the wrong order of size.

example.question: Which is the smallest unit: county, sub-county or ward?
example.correct_answer: Ward

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child has heard the three words but not learned how they nest.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "Sub-county" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Draw the three nested boxes and label them from the outside in; then ask for smallest and largest.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: A county is the biggest. It has sub-counties, and each sub-county has wards. A ward is the smallest.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Thinks a neighbouring county is a sub-county of the learner's own county.

example.question: Kalia County has a neighbour called Mwangaza County. Is Mwangaza one of the sub-counties of Kalia?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it is a sub-county of Kalia
example.correct_answer: No, it is a separate county next to Kalia

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child treats everything nearby as inside the home county.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "Yes, it is a sub-county of Kalia" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Draw two county boxes side by side and a boundary line between them; sub-counties are drawn inside one box only.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: A neighbouring county is a different county. Sub-counties are only the parts inside one county.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Reverses the direction of a neighbour.

example.question: On a map, Kitale County lies north of Meru County. In which direction is Meru County from Kitale County?
example.correct_answer: South

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child repeats the word in the sentence and does not turn round.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "North" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Mark two dots on paper and ask the direction from each dot to the other.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: If Kitale lies north of Meru, then Meru lies south of Kitale.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Calls a county a neighbour when it does not share a boundary with the county.

example.question: Which county is a neighbour of Kalia County, with a shared boundary?
example.correct_answer: The county whose boundary touches Kalia

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child thinks near means next to.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "A county two counties away" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Use a described map: trace the boundary of the county and name only the counties that touch it.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: A neighbour shares a boundary with the county. A county with another county between is not a neighbour.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Thinks the county with more people is the bigger county.

example.question: County A has 3,000 square kilometres and 900,000 people. County B has 12,000 square kilometres and 400,000 people. Which county is larger in size?
example.wrong_answer: County A, because it has more people
example.correct_answer: County B, because its area is larger

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child mixes up how big a place is with how many people live there.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "County A, because it has more people" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Compare a large empty field and a small crowded classroom: which has more space and which has more people?
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: Size is the area of the land in square kilometres. The number of people tells how crowded it is, not how big it is.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..error: Compares numbers by their first digit instead of their size (thinks 800 is more than 3,000 because 8 is more than 3).

example.question: County A is 800 square kilometres and County B is 3,000 square kilometres. Which is larger?
example.correct_answer: County B

SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..cause: The child looks at the first digit and not at the number of digits.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..reveals: Offer "County A" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..help: Write the two numbers in a place value table and compare the thousands first.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..feedback: Compare the whole numbers. 3,000 is more than 800, so County B has the larger area.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Thinks a hill and a mountain are the same or a hill is higher.

example.question: Which is higher, a hill or a mountain?
example.correct_answer: A mountain

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child uses the two words for any raised ground.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "A hill" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Compare Mount Kenya with a small hill near school: describe the height of each.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: A mountain is much higher than a hill. A hill is lower and usually rounded.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Mixes up a river and a lake.

example.question: Which one is water that flows along in a channel?
example.correct_answer: A river

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child knows both have water.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "A lake" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Ask: does the water stay in one place or move on to the sea or a lake?
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: A river flows along a channel. A lake is water that stays in a hollow, with land all round it.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Mixes up a plain and a valley (thinks a valley is wide flat land).

example.question: Which is wide flat land?
example.correct_answer: A plain

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child thinks low land is flat land.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "A valley" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Show a bowl and a flat table: a valley lies between high land on both sides, a plain is wide and flat.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: A plain is wide, flat land. A valley is low land between hills or mountains.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Thinks physical features have no use for people (only beautiful).

example.question: Why is a river important to people near it?
example.wrong_answer: It is only nice to look at
example.correct_answer: It gives water for drinking, farming and fish

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child sees the features as scenery.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "It is only nice to look at" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Ask each learner to name one thing in the day that comes from water or land near home.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: Physical features are useful. Rivers give water and fish, mountains bring rain and visitors, plains give farmland.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Matches a feature to a use it does not have (farming on a lake, fishing on a plain).

example.question: Which feature is best for fishing?
example.correct_answer: A lake

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child guesses from the word and not from what the feature is.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "A plain" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Match each feature to what it is made of: water, high ground, flat land. Then ask what each can give.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: Fish live in water, so lakes, rivers and the sea give fish. Plains are flat dry land, good for farming.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..error: Thinks mountains and valleys only get in the way and do no good.

example.question: How does a mountain help people?
example.correct_answer: It brings rain, rivers and visitors

SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..cause: The child sees only the difficulty of travelling over a mountain.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..reveals: Offer "It only blocks the road" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..help: Trace a river from its source on a mountain to the farms below.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..feedback: Mountains help us. Rain falls on them and feeds rivers, they grow tea and trees, and visitors come to climb them.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Uses spring, summer, autumn and winter as the seasons of the county.

example.question: Which of these is a season in our county?
example.correct_answer: The rainy season

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child has met the four names in picture books from other lands.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "Autumn" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Ask the child to name the weather of each month of the school year, then give each stretch its own name.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Our seasons are hot, cold, dry and rainy. Autumn and winter belong to places far from the equator.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Mixes up the seasons (thinks the rainy season is the hot season, or cold means rain).

example.question: When there is little rain and no clouds for many days, which season is it?
example.correct_answer: The dry season

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child names a season by one feature and not by the whole.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "The rainy season" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Make a weather chart over a week and name the season from what it shows.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: No rain for many days is the dry season. Long rains come about March to May and short rains about October to December.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Treats one day of weather as a whole season.

example.question: It rained on Tuesday. What can we say?
example.wrong_answer: It is now the rainy season
example.correct_answer: It rained that day, and a season lasts for many weeks

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child does not tell weather of a day from a season.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "It is now the rainy season" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Ask what the weather was every day of one month, then name the season.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: One rainy day is weather. A season is the weather that comes for many weeks, month after month.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Thinks farmers should plant when the ground is dry.

example.question: When do farmers plant maize?
example.correct_answer: When the rains begin

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child does not link the seeds to the need for water.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "In the dry season" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Plant two cups of beans, water one, and compare after a week.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Farmers plant when the rains begin, so that the seeds get water. They harvest and dry the crop in the dry season.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Matches a season to an activity that does not fit it (warm sweaters in the hot season).

example.question: What do people wear in the cold season?
example.correct_answer: Warm clothes such as sweaters

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child does not think of the weather of the season.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "Light cotton shirts only" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Ask what the child wears on a cold morning and what on a hot afternoon.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: In the cold season people wear sweaters and jackets. In the hot season they wear light clothes.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Thinks seasons make no difference to what people do.

example.question: Do seasons change what people do?
example.wrong_answer: No, people do the same all year
example.correct_answer: Yes, farmers, traders and travellers change what they do

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child lives in a town and does not see farming.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "No, people do the same all year" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Ask what changes at home when the rains start: crops, roads, clothes, school trips.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Seasons change many things: when farmers plant and harvest, what people wear, sell and how they travel.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Thinks it is safe to run across a wet road to get out of the rain.

example.question: It is raining. What should Njeri do at the road?
example.wrong_answer: Run across fast to get out of the rain
example.correct_answer: Wait at the side and cross only when the road is clear

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child thinks of being dry, not of slippery roads and poor sight.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "Run across fast to get out of the rain" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Role play crossing in the rain: slow, look both ways, hold a friend's hand.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Never run across a road. Rain makes roads slippery and drivers cannot see well. Wait and cross when it is clear.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Thinks it is safe to cross flooded water if it looks shallow.

example.question: A road has water flowing across it after heavy rain. What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Cross if the water looks shallow
example.correct_answer: Do not cross: go back and tell an adult

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child cannot judge how deep or how fast water is.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "Cross if the water looks shallow" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Show a picture of a drift in flood; ask what is hidden under the water.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Never cross flooded water. It may be deep, strong and hide holes. Wait or find another way with an adult.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.error: Thinks rain makes the road safer or that drivers should speed up to get out of the rain.

example.question: How should a driver drive in heavy rain?
example.wrong_answer: Faster, to get out of the rain
example.correct_answer: Slowly, because the road is slippery and it is hard to see

SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.cause: The child links getting home sooner with safety.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.reveals: Offer "Faster, to get out of the rain" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.help: Ask how long it takes to stop on a slippery floor when you run.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.feedback: Rain makes roads slippery, so a vehicle takes longer to stop. A driver must go slowly.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..error: Mixes up a museum and a monument.

example.question: Which place keeps and shows old objects and records?
example.correct_answer: A museum

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..cause: The child treats all old built places as the same thing.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..reveals: Offer "A monument" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..help: Ask: where do you go inside to see old tools and pictures, and what do you pass in a town square that remembers a person?
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..feedback: A museum keeps and shows old objects. A monument is a structure built to remember a person or an event.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..error: Thinks any big or famous new building is a historic built environment.

example.question: Which is a historic built environment?
example.correct_answer: An old fort that still stands

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..cause: The child thinks big or famous means historic.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..reveals: Offer "A new shopping mall" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..help: Ask for the date of each place and what it tells about the past.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..feedback: A historic place is old and tells about the past. A new mall is not historic, however big it is.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..error: Thinks a cultural centre is a market or a shop.

example.question: What is a cultural centre?
example.wrong_answer: A place to buy and sell goods
example.correct_answer: A place that shows the way of life of communities

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..cause: The child links "centre" with a shopping centre.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..reveals: Offer "A place to buy and sell goods" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..help: Ask what you might see and do at a cultural centre: dances, houses, crafts, food.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..feedback: A cultural centre shows the traditions of communities, such as dance, food, dress and crafts.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..error: Thinks old places should be pulled down because they are old.

example.question: An old fort is crumbling. What should the county do?
example.wrong_answer: Pull it down and build a new shop
example.correct_answer: Repair and protect it because it tells our history

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..cause: The child values only what is new.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..reveals: Offer "Pull it down and build a new shop" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..help: Ask what a grandmother's stories give that a new book does not, then link this to old places.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..feedback: Historic places cannot be rebuilt once they are gone. They teach history and keep our identity, so we protect them.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..error: Thinks historic places matter only for the money from visitors.

example.question: Why do we keep museums and monuments?
example.wrong_answer: Only to earn money from visitors
example.correct_answer: To learn about the past and keep our identity, and visitors also bring income

SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..cause: The child sees one reason where there are several.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..reveals: Offer "Only to earn money from visitors" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..help: Brainstorm three reasons for keeping a place; mark which are about learning and which about income.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..feedback: Visitors bring income, but the first reasons are learning about the past and keeping the identity of the community.
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..error: Thinks a family can make or grow everything it needs.

example.question: Can one family grow, make and do everything it needs?
example.correct_answer: No, so people depend on each other

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..cause: The child sees one family in the home, not the work of others behind each thing.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..reveals: Offer "Yes, if it works hard" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..help: List what a family uses in one day and who made each thing.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..feedback: No family can do everything. People depend on farmers, traders, health workers and many others.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..error: Thinks only one side depends on the other (the shopkeeper does not need the farmer).

example.question: A farmer sells vegetables to a shopkeeper. Who needs the other?
example.wrong_answer: Only the farmer needs the shopkeeper
example.correct_answer: Both need each other

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..cause: The child sees the farmer as the one with the problem.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..reveals: Offer "Only the farmer needs the shopkeeper" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..help: Ask what the shopkeeper sells if no farmers sell to him, and what the farmer does if there is no shop.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..feedback: Each needs the other. The farmer needs a market, and the shopkeeper needs goods to sell.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..error: Matches a worker or place to the wrong service (a hospital for food, a church for medicine).

example.question: What does a hospital give people?
example.correct_answer: Care for the sick

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..cause: The child guesses from the building and not from what it does.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..reveals: Offer "Food to eat" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..help: Make a matching chart of five places and what they give.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..feedback: A hospital gives care for the sick. A farm gives food, and a place of worship gives spiritual guidance.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..error: Thinks needing other people is a weakness or a bad thing.

example.question: Is it bad to depend on other people?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, strong people do things alone
example.correct_answer: No, it lets everyone use their skills and gain more

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..cause: The child equates depending on others with being unable.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..reveals: Offer "Yes, strong people do things alone" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..help: Ask who made the school desk, who grew the lunch and who taught the lesson.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..feedback: Depending on each other is a strength. We get what we cannot make and share what we can.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..error: Thinks the only benefit of trade or sharing is money.

example.question: What do people get when they depend on each other?
example.correct_answer: Goods and services they cannot make and also friendship and income

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..cause: The child links trade only to cash.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..reveals: Offer "Only money" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..help: Ask what a neighbour who lends a tool gives that is not money.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..feedback: People get goods, services, skills, income and friendship. Money is only one benefit.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.error: Mixes up population distribution with the total number of people.

example.question: What does population distribution mean?
example.wrong_answer: The total number of people in a county
example.correct_answer: How people are spread over an area

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.reveals: Offer "The total number of people in a county" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.help: Place twelve counters on a page: first all in one corner, then spread out; the total is the same.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.feedback: Distribution is how people are spread over the area. The total number is a different thing.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.error: Thinks a dense area is a large area.

example.question: An area has many people living close together. Is it dense or sparse?
example.correct_answer: Dense

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.cause: The child links dense with large size or fills the word with a different meaning.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.reveals: Offer "Sparse" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.help: Compare ten learners in a small room and ten on a football pitch.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.feedback: Dense means many people in a small space. Sparse means few people spread over a large space.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.error: Gives reasons the wrong way round (people crowd into very dry, steep or unsafe places).

example.question: Why do many people live near a river with good soil and rain?
example.wrong_answer: Because there is no water there
example.correct_answer: Because they get water, food and work there

SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.cause: The child does not link where people live with what the land gives.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.reveals: Offer "Because there is no water there" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.help: Ask what the family needs each day and where they find it.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.feedback: People live where they can get water, food, work, roads and safety. Dry, steep, flooded or unsafe places have few people.
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..error: Sorts an example under the wrong aspect (a drum under dressing, ugali under housing).

example.question: Under which aspect of culture is a kiondo (a sisal basket)?
example.correct_answer: Artefacts

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..cause: The child sorts by the first thing that comes to mind.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..reveals: Offer "Dressing" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..help: Make six boxes, one for each aspect, and sort a pile of picture cards.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..feedback: A kiondo is made by hand, so it is an artefact. Clothes are dressing, ugali is food, a manyatta is housing.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..error: Thinks traditional culture belongs only to the past or only to old people.

example.question: Is traditional culture still practised today?
example.correct_answer: Yes, many people still practise it

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..cause: The child sees culture as something in a museum.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..reveals: Offer "No, it is finished" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..help: Ask which dishes, songs and ceremonies the family still shares.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..feedback: Culture is alive. People still practise many traditions, in food, dress, songs, games and ceremonies.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..error: Thinks all communities in a county have the same traditions.

example.question: Do all the communities in a county have the same traditions?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, they all do the same things
example.correct_answer: No, each community has its own as well as shared ones

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..cause: The child knows only the home community well.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..reveals: Offer "Yes, they all do the same things" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..help: Ask each learner to name one dish, dance or dress from their own community.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..feedback: Communities differ in dress, food, houses and ceremonies, and respecting the differences keeps us at peace.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.error: Names the wrong value for a situation (calls handing in lost money respect, not honesty).

example.question: Wekesa finds a lost shilling coin and hands it to the teacher. Which value does he show?
example.correct_answer: Honesty

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.cause: The child knows the words and does not tie them to actions.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.reveals: Offer "Hard work" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.help: Make cards of the value words and match them to six short scenes.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.feedback: Handing in what is not yours is honesty. Respect is speaking and acting kindly to others.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.error: Thinks values are the same as rules or punishments.

example.question: Which is a value of a school?
example.correct_answer: Respect

SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.cause: The child links school with rules and punishments.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.reveals: Offer "The cane" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.help: Ask the child what a value is: a good idea that guides us, even without a teacher watching.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.feedback: A value is a belief about what is good, such as respect or honesty. Rules and punishments are different.
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.M_SC.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..error: Calls a thing made by people a natural resource (a building, a road).

example.question: Which is a natural resource?
example.correct_answer: A river

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..cause: The child counts every useful thing as natural.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..reveals: Offer "A road" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..help: Sort a list into things that were here before people and things people built.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..feedback: Natural resources are given by nature: soil, water, forests, minerals and wildlife. Roads and buildings are made by people.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..error: Calls play or rest an economic activity (or does not see farming as one).

example.question: Which is an economic activity?
example.correct_answer: Selling vegetables at the market

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..cause: The child counts every kind of activity.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..reveals: Offer "Playing football after school" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..help: Ask whether the activity gives food, goods or an income.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..feedback: An economic activity gives goods, services or an income, such as farming, fishing and trading.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..error: Matches an activity to the wrong resource (fishing for a forest, mining for water).

example.question: Which resource does fishing use?
example.correct_answer: Lakes, rivers or the sea

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..cause: The child guesses from the word and not from the product.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..reveals: Offer "Forests" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..help: Ask: what does the activity bring in? Then ask where it comes from.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..feedback: Fishing uses water, in lakes, rivers or the sea. Mining uses minerals, and lumbering uses forests.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..error: Thinks economic activities help only rich people.

example.question: Who gains from farming in a county?
example.correct_answer: Farmers, workers, traders and everyone who eats

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..cause: The child links activity to the wealth of the owner.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..reveals: Offer "Only rich people" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..help: Trace a loaf of bread from the farm to the table and name the people who gain at each step.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..feedback: Many people gain: the farmer, the worker, the trader and every person who buys food.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..error: Thinks activities give only food, not jobs, income or raw materials.

example.question: Which is a reason that mining matters to a county?
example.correct_answer: It gives jobs, income and raw materials

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..cause: The child gives the answer for farming to every activity.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..reveals: Offer "It gives food" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..help: Make a table of five activities and what each gives.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..feedback: Activities give jobs, income and raw materials, and some give food. Mining gives jobs and minerals.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Swaps the raw material and the product (thinks sugar is the raw material for sugarcane).

example.question: What is the raw material in a sugar factory?
example.correct_answer: Sugarcane

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child names the thing he or she knows best.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "Sugar" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: Use pairs: before the factory and after the factory.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: The raw material goes in. Sugarcane goes into the factory and sugar comes out.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Calls a shop or a farm an industry.

example.question: Which place is an industry?
example.correct_answer: A factory that turns sugarcane into sugar

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child thinks any busy business is an industry.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "A shop that sells sugar" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: Ask: does this place make something new from something else?
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: An industry makes or processes goods. A shop only sells goods and a farm grows the raw materials.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Thinks only the owner gains from an industry.

example.question: Who gains when a factory opens in a county?
example.correct_answer: Workers, farmers, shoppers and the county

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child sees the owner as the only person involved.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "Only the owner" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: List who works at a milk factory, who sells it the milk and who buys the milk.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: Workers get jobs, farmers get a market, shoppers get goods and the county gets money.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Lists pollution or noise as a benefit.

example.question: Which is a benefit of an industry?
example.correct_answer: Jobs for people in the county

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child does not tell a benefit from a problem.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "Dirty smoke from the chimney" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: Sort a list into "good for people" and "problem to solve".
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: Jobs, income and goods are benefits. Smoke and waste are problems that industries must control.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Thinks an industry can be built anywhere with no reason.

example.question: Why is a sugar factory built near sugarcane farms?
example.wrong_answer: Because there is no reason, any place does
example.correct_answer: Because the heavy cane is cheap to carry a short way

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child does not link the place to the cost or ease of work.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "Because there is no reason, any place does" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: Ask the child to carry a heavy bag a short way and a long way.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: Factories are placed near raw materials, workers, roads, water and a market, so that costs are lower.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..error: Places an industry far from its raw material (a milk factory far from dairy farms).

example.question: Where is the best place for a milk factory?
example.correct_answer: Near the dairy farms, with good roads

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..cause: The child thinks only about the buyer, not about milk that goes bad.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..reveals: Offer "Far from any dairy farms" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..help: Ask what happens to fresh milk after a day in the sun.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..feedback: Milk goes bad quickly, so the factory is near the farms, on a good road.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..error: Chooses a project that needs what the school does not have (fish ponds with no water).

example.question: A school has a dry field and no water tank. Which project suits it best?
example.correct_answer: Keeping bees or planting drought-resistant trees

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..cause: The child picks the most exciting project and does not check what is needed.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..reveals: Offer "Fish farming" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..help: List what each project needs and tick what the school has.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..feedback: Choose a project that suits your land, water, money and people. Fish need water.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..error: Thinks a project needs no plan, just start.

example.question: What should a school do before starting a project?
example.wrong_answer: Start at once with no plan
example.correct_answer: Make a plan of work, materials and who does what

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..cause: The child links enterprise with action only.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..reveals: Offer "Start at once with no plan" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..help: Plan a class lunch together: who brings what, and what does it cost?
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..feedback: A project needs a plan: what to do, the materials, the people, the cost and the time.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..error: Thinks a leader can keep the money the project makes.

example.question: The class sold vegetables and made 500 shillings. What should the treasurer do?
example.correct_answer: Record it and keep it safely for the project

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..cause: The child sees money as belonging to whoever holds it.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..reveals: Offer "Keep it for himself" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..help: Role play the treasurer with a record book and a locked box.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..feedback: Project money belongs to the project and the school. Keep it safe and record every shilling.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..error: Thinks a mistake or a loss should be hidden to avoid blame.

example.question: A group loses some money by mistake. What is right?
example.wrong_answer: Hide it so no one is blamed
example.correct_answer: Report it honestly and learn from it

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..reveals: Offer "Hide it so no one is blamed" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..help: Practise saying "we lost it, and here is what we will do".
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..feedback: Honest groups report their mistakes and lose less over time. Hiding them breaks trust.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..error: Thinks one strong leader should do all the work or decide everything.

example.question: How should a project team decide?
example.correct_answer: The team shares ideas and decides together

SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..cause: The child sees leadership as control.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..reveals: Offer "The leader decides everything alone" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..help: Ask the team to decide where to keep the tools, then compare it with one person deciding.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..feedback: Teams share the work and the decisions, so everyone takes part and feels the project belongs to them.
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..error: Thinks only learners with the top marks are good citizens.

example.question: Who is a good citizen in school?
example.wrong_answer: Only the learner with the top marks
example.correct_answer: Any learner who is respectful, honest and helpful

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..cause: The child links a good learner with good marks.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..reveals: Offer "Only the learner with the top marks" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..help: Ask what a learner can do for others even with low marks.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..feedback: A good citizen shows qualities such as respect, honesty and helpfulness. Marks are different from character.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..error: Thinks a good citizen only keeps quiet and obeys, never speaks up.

example.question: Which learner is a good citizen?
example.correct_answer: The one who keeps fair rules and helps others, and speaks up kindly when something is wrong

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..cause: The child links good with silent.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..reveals: Offer "The one who never speaks" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..help: Role play a learner who sees someone bullied: what is the good action?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..feedback: A good citizen follows fair rules, cares for others, and politely speaks up when something is wrong.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..error: Thinks telling a teacher about bullying is wrong (telling tales).

example.question: You see a learner being bullied. What does a good citizen do?
example.wrong_answer: Say nothing, because telling tales is wrong
example.correct_answer: Tell a teacher and help the learner

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..cause: The child confuses reporting harm with gossip.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..reveals: Offer "Say nothing, because telling tales is wrong" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..help: Ask: is it gossip to tell a teacher that someone is being hurt?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..feedback: Telling a teacher about harm is not telling tales. A good citizen helps keep everyone safe.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.error: Thinks peace means nobody ever disagrees.

example.question: What does peace mean in school?
example.correct_answer: Settling disagreements without hurting anyone

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.cause: The child sees peace as quiet.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.reveals: Offer "Nobody ever disagrees" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.help: Ask for a time when two friends disagreed and still stayed friends.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.feedback: People will sometimes disagree. Peace is settling it with respect and without harm.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_NO_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.error: Thinks peace comes from fear and punishment.

example.question: What keeps a school peaceful?
example.correct_answer: Respect, fairness and listening

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.cause: The child links order with punishment.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.reveals: Offer "Fear of strict punishment" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.help: Compare a class that is quiet for the cane and a class that is kind by choice.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.feedback: Peace grows from respect, fairness, sharing and forgiveness, not from fear.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_THR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.error: Thinks spreading talk about others or taking sides helps peace.

example.question: Which action breaks peace?
example.correct_answer: Spreading rumours about a classmate

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.cause: The child does not see how talk hurts.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.reveals: Offer "Listening to both sides" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.help: Pass a message along a line and watch it change.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.feedback: Rumours and name-calling break peace. Listening, honesty and kind words keep it.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.M_PE_GOS.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.error: Thinks hitting back or revenge settles a quarrel.

example.question: A classmate pushes you by mistake. What is the peaceful reply?
example.correct_answer: Stay calm and say what happened

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.cause: The child thinks strength ends a quarrel.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.reveals: Offer "Push back harder" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.help: Role play both: what happens after a push back, and after a calm word?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.feedback: Hitting back makes a quarrel bigger. Stay calm, talk, and ask a teacher to help if needed.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.error: Thinks pretending the problem is not there is the best way, and never speaking again.

example.question: Two friends quarrelled. What is the best way to settle it?
example.wrong_answer: Never speak to each other again
example.correct_answer: Talk about it, say sorry and forgive

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.cause: The child thinks silence ends a quarrel.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.reveals: Offer "Never speak to each other again" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.help: Ask how the friendship feels after a week of silence.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.feedback: Silence does not settle a quarrel. Talk, listen, say sorry and forgive.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.error: Puts the steps of settling a quarrel in the wrong order (apologise before listening).

example.question: What comes first when settling a quarrel?
example.wrong_answer: Shout until the other gives in
example.correct_answer: Calm down and listen

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.cause: The child does not think of steps.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.reveals: Offer "Shout until the other gives in" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.help: Write the steps on cards and order them: calm, listen, talk, say sorry, forgive.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.feedback: First calm down and listen. Then talk about it, say sorry and forgive. A mediator can help.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.M_PE_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.error: Thinks beating a child is only discipline and never abuse.

example.question: A teacher beats a learner until he is hurt. Is this child abuse?
example.correct_answer: Yes, hurting a child is abuse

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.cause: The child has seen beating treated as normal.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.reveals: Offer "No, it is only discipline" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.help: Ask: does discipline teach with care or hurt? Discuss other ways, such as talking and fair consequences.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.feedback: Hurting a child is abuse. Discipline teaches without harming the child.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.error: Thinks any work a child does is fine (or that all chores are child labour).

example.question: Which is child labour?
example.correct_answer: Working all day in a quarry instead of going to school

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.cause: The child does not tell light chores from harmful work.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.reveals: Offer "Washing a plate after supper" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.help: Sort examples by: safe, short, does not stop school, does not harm.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.feedback: Light chores that do not stop school or harm the child are fine. Heavy or dangerous work that stops school is child labour.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.error: Thinks only beating counts as child abuse.

example.question: Which of these is child abuse?
example.correct_answer: Forcing a girl to marry early

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.cause: The child knows only the form seen most often.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.reveals: Offer "Only beating a child" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.help: List six forms and ask: how does each harm the child?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.feedback: Child abuse takes many forms: forced marriage, labour, trafficking, neglect and sexual abuse, as well as beating.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.M_C.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.error: Thinks a child causes the abuse by bad behaviour.

example.question: Why was a child abused by an adult?
example.correct_answer: The adult chose to harm the child

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.cause: The child has heard "you made me do it".
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.reveals: Offer "The child behaved badly" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.help: Ask: can anything a child does make it right for an adult to hurt him or her?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.feedback: Abuse is never the child's fault. The adult is responsible for the harm.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.error: Thinks a custom or tradition makes an abuse acceptable.

example.question: Some say a harmful custom is fine because it is old. What is right?
example.wrong_answer: It is fine if it is a tradition
example.correct_answer: A custom that harms a child must stop

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.cause: The child respects elders and customs.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.reveals: Offer "It is fine if it is a tradition" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.help: Discuss that culture changes, and that keeping children safe is also a tradition.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.feedback: No custom makes harm to a child right. Many customs are good, but harmful ones must stop.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.error: Thinks children forget abuse and are not changed by it.

example.question: What can child abuse do to a child?
example.correct_answer: It can hurt the body, cause fear and make the child leave school

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.cause: The child thinks harm only shows on the body.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.reveals: Offer "Nothing, children forget" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.help: List ways a bad experience at school changes how a learner feels.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.feedback: Abuse can injure, frighten and make a child sad, sick or leave school.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.error: Thinks a hurt child or a friend should keep it secret.

example.question: A friend tells you an adult is hurting him. What should you do?
example.correct_answer: Tell a trusted adult such as a teacher, or call Childline on 116

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.cause: The child fears trouble or being a tell-tale.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.reveals: Offer "Keep it a secret" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.help: Make a list of the adults who keep children safe and practise saying "I need to tell you something".
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.feedback: Never keep harm secret. Tell a trusted adult, or call Childline on 116, which is free.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.M.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.error: Thinks a leader chosen by the teacher is an election.

example.question: Which way of choosing a head prefect is democratic?
example.correct_answer: All learners vote

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.cause: The child thinks any choosing is an election.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.reveals: Offer "The teacher picks a favourite" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.help: Compare: who chose? how many people had a say?
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.feedback: In an election all voters have a say. A teacher choosing alone is appointing.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.error: Puts election steps in the wrong order (voting before the campaign).

example.question: Which comes first in a school election?
example.correct_answer: Nominating the candidates

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.cause: The child remembers voting and counting only.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.reveals: Offer "Counting the votes" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.help: Order the steps on cards: nominate, campaign, vote, count, announce.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.feedback: The order is nomination, campaign, voting, counting and announcing the winner.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.error: Thinks the loudest or most popular learner wins by right.

example.question: How should a winner be decided?
example.correct_answer: By counting the votes of everyone

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.cause: The child links winning with being strong.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.reveals: Offer "The loudest learner wins" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.help: Hold a vote on a class song and count each hand.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.feedback: The winner is the candidate with the most votes, counted fairly.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_BE.error: Thinks those who lose a vote have no say and no value.

example.question: After a vote, what happens to the views of those who lost?
example.correct_answer: They are still respected

SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_BE.cause: The child sees the vote as a win or loss only.
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_BE.reveals: Offer "They are ignored" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.

example.correct_answer: Learners elected by their classmates
